steps.title: Plan the interval at the destination root: accept and move in one change
steps.detail: A migrated account is added to the root of the new organization; it reaches OU Payments (ou-fern-pay1) only when the destination management account moves it there. Until then only the policies attached to the root apply. Not in force during that interval: SCP Fernhill-EU-Only-Regions at OU Business Units (ou-fern-bu); SCP aws-guardrails-kjwqpf at OU Business Units (ou-fern-bu); RCP Fernhill-Block-External-Principals at OU Business Units (ou-fern-bu); BACKUP Fernhill-Core-Backups at OU Business Units (ou-fern-bu); SCP Fernhill-Payments-Controls at OU Payments (ou-fern-pay1); TAG Fernhill-Payments-Cost-Centers at OU Payments (ou-fern-pay1). OU Payments (ou-fern-pay1) is registered with Control Tower; at the root the account is not governed and cannot be enrolled. Of the actions in use, 15 are allowed at the root and denied at the target position, so the account can still perform them in the interval: cloudwatch:PutMetricData, dynamodb:*, ec2:CreateTransitGatewayVpcAttachment, ec2:CreateVpc, ec2:DescribeInstances, ec2:RunInstances, ec2:TerminateInstances, kms:Decrypt, lambda:InvokeFunction, logs:CreateLogGroup, rds:CreateDBInstance, rds:DescribeDBInstances, s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject, secretsmanager:GetSecretValue. 4 inbound request(s) that the target position denies are still admitted at the root: kms:Decrypt by arn:aws:iam::111111111118:role/DataPlatformIngest; s3:GetObject by 999999999999; s3:ListBucket by 999999999999; sts:AssumeRole by arn:aws:iam::111111111118:role/DataPlatformIngest. Move the account in the same change as the acceptance, and treat anything done in between as done without the target OU's guardrails. The verdict board evaluates the target position; this finding is the root position. The move step that follows the acceptance in this runbook closes the interval; have the destination management account ready to run it as soon as the account has joined.

steps.title: Move stack payments-api off the shared networking before the account leaves
steps.detail: It references subnet-e056c922dbb17986a, subnet-1d0f03c495e44a0e4 (parameter AppSubnetIds), shared by account 111111111112 with organization o-larkspur0001. What the documentation says happens when the share ends: existing participant resources continue to run in the subnet; no new resources can be created in it, while existing ones can still be modified, described and deleted (subnets can only be shared inside one organization). The stack contains AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup, which launches instances into its subnets whenever it scales or replaces one. Those launches need to create resources in the subnet, which fails once the share ends: what is running keeps running, and nothing can be replaced or scaled out. A stack update that replaces a resource in the subnet fails for the same reason. Sharing them again is not a way out: this resource type can only be shared inside one organization, so the workload has to move to networking of the destination before the account leaves. Redeploying the stack with subnets and attachments the account owns, or that the destination shares with it, is the fix; the parameters named above are where the stack takes them from.

steps.detail: The reference uses Fn::GetStackOutput through role arn:aws:iam::111111111113:role/CfnOutputReader in account 111111111113, which stays in organization o-larkspur0001. It is a weak reference: the value is resolved when the consuming stack is created or updated and nothing changes at the moment of the move. The next update of payments-api resolves it again, across organizations by then: CloudFormation's execution role in this account has to assume arn:aws:iam::111111111113:role/CfnOutputReader, which the role's trust policy (in the other account, not collected here), the destination's SCPs on this account and the RCPs of the role's organization decide. The sts:AssumeRole call was evaluated as a derived operation: see the SCP and RCP checks for a denial. If the value changes or the producing stack is deleted, this stack is not told; plan where the value comes from once the accounts are in different organizations. Either keep the reference (the role's trust policy has to admit this account by ID rather than by organization) or replace it with a parameter that carries the value.

steps.title: Re-share larkspur-core-network with the account directly: ec2:Subnet, ec2:TransitGateway, route53resolver:ResolverRule
steps.detail: Owner 111111111112 shares larkspur-core-network (ec2:Subnet, ec2:TransitGateway, route53resolver:ResolverRule) with arn:aws:organizations::111111111111:organization/o-larkspur0001 today. After the move those principals no longer cover the account. Ask the owner to add account 111111111115 as a principal before the move so nothing attached to these resources is interrupted. The account will be outside the organization, so the share has to allow external principals and the account has to accept an invitation. The documentation says traffic or a declared operation stops with this share, so the move stays NO-GO until it is done: Shared by account 111111111112 with organization o-larkspur0001. It is scoped to the source organization or one of its OUs and stops applying when the account leaves. What the documentation says happens: ec2:Subnet: existing participant resources continue to run in the subnet; no new resources can be created in it, while existing ones can still be modified, described and deleted (subnets can only be shared inside one organization). steps.title: Delete the role that lets 111111111111 into the account, and give Fernhill Group (o-fernhill0001) its own
steps.detail: The account was created in the source organization, which created an IAM role (OrganizationAccountAccessRole unless another name was given) that the source management account can assume. When an account leaves an organization, any IAM role that was created to give the organization's management account access is not deleted.
